brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CET on 4 November; new research covers 17:10 CET on 3 November to 05:10 CET on 4 November, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Zelensky Honors Melania Trump as Russian and Ukrainian Envoys Head to the White House
items.lede: Ukraine gave the US first lady its top award for women after a ceasefire she helped broker let several hundred people leave occupied Oleshky.

sections.text: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky awarded US first lady Melania Trump the Order of Princess Olga, 1st Class, BBC News reported [1][2]. The decree cited her personal contribution to humanitarian support for Ukraine [1]. The award followed the end of a ceasefire in the Kherson region that allowed several hundred people to leave Russian-occupied Oleshky [1]. The White House said Melania Trump independently started contacts between the two sides and secured the ceasefire [1]. Russian and Ukrainian delegations, including both countries' human rights ombudsmen, are due at the White House on Thursday at her invitation [1]. Neither side detailed the extent of her role [1].
Confidence is high on the award and the planned meeting, which BBC News and the Kyiv Independent report from the decree and White House statements.

items.title: China Says It Is Preparing a Possible Xi-Trump-Putin Meeting in Shenzhen
items.lede: Europeans worry that any talks on Russia's war on Ukraine there could exclude Kyiv, while the Kremlin called the idea very useful.

sections.text: China is in talks with Russia and the United States on a possible meeting of Xi Jinping, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said Wednesday [3]. The meeting would take place at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, POLITICO Europe reported [3]. Spokesperson Mao Ning did not say what the leaders would discuss [3]. Trump said last month he wanted to discuss denuclearization in such a format, "not so much" Ukraine [3]. Germany's President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said Xi rejected discussing Ukraine in that format [3]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called such a meeting "appropriate and very useful" [3].
Confidence is moderate: the talks rest on a Chinese official statement reported by one outlet, and no date or agenda is fixed.

items.title: Ukraine's Anti-Graft Bureau Says SBU Officials Shielded Scam Call Centers
items.lede: NABU said a senior Security Service official threatened to use a firearm to obstruct searches carried out under a court warrant.

sections.text: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and the anti-corruption prosecutor said on 4 November they had exposed a group that bribed senior law enforcement officials [4]. They said the bribes bought protection for scam call centers and other illegal businesses [4]. The scheme allegedly involved senior officials of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU), the National Police, and the Prosecutor General's Office [4]. NABU searched SBU officials' premises under a High Anti-Corruption Court warrant [4]. The bureau said a senior SBU official obstructed the searches and threatened to use a firearm [4]. The case grows out of a September probe that brought down Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko, who later fled Ukraine [4]. No SBU response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the claims come from the investigating agencies, relayed by one outlet, and the SBU had not responded.

items.title: Death Toll From Russia's Bombing of a Ukrainian Aid Center Rises to 40
items.lede: Zelensky said 40 people are now confirmed dead in Komyshuvakha, with more than 30 feared still under the rubble on the third day of searches.

sections.text: At least 26 people were killed when Russian aerial bombs hit an aid distribution center in Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, on Monday [5]. Regional head Mykhailo Semikin said at least nine 3,000-kilogram bombs hit the village [5]. He said five people were injured and 27 were initially reported missing [5]. Zelensky said more than 50 people could still be under the rubble [6][7]. Russia's Defense Ministry said the strike targeted Ukrainian military units and killed 25 servicemen, the BBC reported [7]. The BBC said it found no credible evidence of military use of the site [7]. Ukrainian officials put the toll at 37 earlier on 4 November, as searches entered a third day, Interfax-Ukraine reported [8]. Russia used a 3-ton FAB-3000 bomb, the Kyiv Independent reported [9]. Local authorities said Wednesday morning that 59 people were considered missing [9]. Later on Wednesday, Zelensky said 40 people were confirmed dead and more than 30 might still be under the rubble, the Guardian reported [10].

Confidence is high on the strike and the rising toll, which BBC News, the Kyiv Independent, and the Guardian attribute to Ukrainian officials. The toll may still change. Russia's claim of a military target is unsupported.

items.title: Russia Keeps Hitting Ukraine's Power Grid After the Year's Biggest Energy Strike
items.lede: New strikes hit energy sites in six more regions within a day, and Zelensky said repeated attacks are slowing repairs.

sections.text: Russia launched its biggest mass attack on Ukraine's energy facilities this year overnight into Tuesday, the Kyiv Independent reported [11]. Strikes hit substations, transmission lines, and power plants in 10 regions and cut power to households [11]. Ukrenergo chief Vitalii Zaichenko said it was one of the largest ballistic missile waves on critical infrastructure [11]. Ukraine's air force said Russia fired ballistic missiles, 59 cruise missiles, and 289 attack drones [12]. A morning missile strike on Dnipro killed two people and injured 20, regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said [12]. Regional authorities said Russian attacks killed at least 38 people and injured 167 over the past day [12]. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said strikes on the regional distribution network caused emergency power cuts and water outages in Kyiv [13]. Over the following day, Russian attacks killed six people and injured 50 across Ukraine, local authorities said [14]. Strikes hit energy sites in the Odesa, Kirovohrad, Zhytomyr, Ternopil, Volyn, and Rivne regions [14]. DTEK said emergency outages were introduced in several regions, including Kyiv [14]. Zelensky said repeated strikes and constant air raid alerts are making repairs take much longer [14].
Confidence is high on the scale and damage, which the Kyiv Independent attributes to named Ukrainian officials and companies. Casualty totals are preliminary.

items.title: Drone Hits an Ozon Warehouse in Russia's Adygea Republic
items.lede: The online retailer said a fire broke out and staff were evacuated, with no injuries reported so far.

sections.text: A drone struck an Ozon logistics center in Russia's Adygea Republic overnight into 4 November, the company said in a statement reported by the Kyiv Independent [15]. Ozon said it evacuated all employees, no one was injured, and a fire broke out [15]. The company said goods in the warehouse were pulled from its online store [15]. Adygea's head, Murat Kumpilov, later said a drone attack caused a fire at the Ozon logistics center in Adygeysk and no casualties were reported, RIA Novosti reported [16]. No Ukrainian claim of responsibility was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Russian sources, the company and Adygea's head, relayed by the Kyiv Independent and Russian state media.

items.title: Ukraine Charges Zelensky's Former Spokeswoman Iuliia Mendel With Treason
items.lede: The SBU and prosecutors filed the charges in absentia, accusing Mendel, now a critic of Zelensky, of spreading pro-Kremlin narratives during martial law.

sections.text: Ukraine's Security Service and the Prosecutor General's Office served Iuliia Mendel in absentia with a notice of suspicion of treason on 3 November [17][18]. The agencies accused her of "information and subversive activities against Ukraine" and of justifying Russia's war [17]. Mendel was Zelensky's press secretary from 2019 to 2021 and later became a vocal critic who called him a "dictator" [17]. In May she appeared on Tucker Carlson's podcast, and in September she spoke at a side event at the invitation of Germany's AfD party [17]. Prosecutors said the case rests on her public statements, including the Carlson interview, and cited treason committed under martial law [18]. Mendel said the case was based on her public statements in Western media and on social media, and she denied any collaboration with Russia, the Kyiv Independent reported [17].

Confidence is high that the charges were filed, based on the Prosecutor General's Office statement and the Kyiv Independent; Mendel denies the allegations; the allegations are unproven and the evidence is not public.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Hackers Take Over a Ukrainian News Site and Email Readers Fake Claims
items.lede: The Kyiv Independent said attackers reached its website and a newsletter service, in a breach resembling the hack of Ukraine's air raid alert app.

sections.text: Ukraine's Kyiv Independent said it came under a cyberattack on 4 November that disrupted its website [1]. Hackers gained access to its content management system and to a newsletter service [1]. They sent four emails and posted similar messages with fake claims in Russian and English, which staff deleted [1]. The outlet said the content points to a Russian operation [1]. It said the attack resembled the hack of Ukraine's air raid alert app three days earlier [1]. Editor-in-chief Olga Rudenko said it was the first such attack on the outlet [1]. The outlet said readers' payment data were not at risk [1]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the breach is the outlet's own account, and the Russian attribution is its assessment, not an official finding.

items.title: Montenegro and Albania Ask NATO for Help Against Russian Disinformation
items.lede: Defense ministers in Podgorica and Tirana want alliance expert teams to counter online campaigns they say aim to destabilize the Western Balkans.

sections.text: Montenegrin Defense Minister Dragan Krapović and Albanian Defense Minister Ermal Nufi asked NATO to step up support against Russian disinformation, POLITICO Europe reported [2]. "Russia is continuously conducting ... information campaigns that are aimed at vulnerabilities of the Montenegrin and other societies in the Western Balkans," Krapović said [2][3]. Nufi said Albania had seen a rise in social media campaigns "fueling hatred and anger" over the past year [2]. Three NATO diplomats said allies would be open to sending a hybrid response team, which typically requires consensus [2]. A NATO official said the alliance "can provide further support, when requested" [2]. Current Time, run by RFE/RL, also reported the request [4].
Confidence is high on the ministers' request, which POLITICO Europe obtained in interviews and Vijesti and Current Time followed up. Whether NATO sends a team is not decided.

items.title: German Police Arrest a Third Suspect Over Arson on a Starlink Terminal in Poland
items.lede: Prosecutors in Stuttgart say the Turkish citizen arrested near Reutlingen hired two men already held for the 23 September attack.

sections.text: German special police units arrested a Turkish citizen in the Reutlingen district of Baden-Württemberg on 3 November, the Stuttgarter Zeitung reported [5]. The arrest is linked to an arson attack on a satellite internet terminal in Poland on 23 September [5]. Two suspects were arrested in Nürtingen on 12 October and remain in custody [5]. Investigators say the new suspect gave the two men the job [5]. Police seized eight phones and ammunition [5]. A Stuttgart judge issued an arrest warrant on suspicion of preparing a terrorist offense [5]. The case is led by the state security center at the Stuttgart prosecutor general's office and the state criminal police [5]. No motive or sponsor was named by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one newspaper's report of the prosecutors' statement, and the charges are unproven.

items.title: Fridge Hackers Hit France's Blood Service as Attacks on European Stores Spread
items.lede: France's blood agency said attackers raised temperatures at three cold stores, but alarms let staff act before blood products were harmed.

sections.text: A cyberattack early Monday hit fridges and freezers in dozens of European supermarkets [6]. No one had claimed responsibility, AFP said [7]. The BBC said Tuesday that supermarkets in 10 countries, including Germany, had reported problems [8]. About 40 Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected [6]. Belgian federal prosecutors opened a criminal investigation [9][10]. EU Agriculture Commissioner Christophe Hansen called the attacks a deliberate attempt to disrupt the EU food supply [11]. France's national blood service, EFS, said hackers raised temperature and defrost settings to very high levels at three cold stores overnight into Monday [12][13]. EFS said alarms let technicians step in before blood products were compromised [12]. Retailers in Italy, Germany, Romania, and Britain were also hit on Tuesday, the Guardian reported [12]. Dutch-Belgian group Ahold Delhaize said its Delhaize unit was hit again this week [14]. Lithuania's five largest supermarket chains told LRT their stores were not affected [15].

Confidence is high on the attacks, the countries hit, and the French blood service incident, which several major outlets report from official and company statements. No one has claimed responsibility.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: Paris Police Ban the Unions' Bastille Route for Thursday's General Strike
items.lede: France's government says it will not allow a repeat of the 17 October violence as unions, students, and yellow vests prepare nationwide strikes.

sections.text: Paris police banned the Bastille-to-Concorde route that unions filed for Thursday's national strike and offered a République-to-Nation route instead, BFMTV reported [1]. The unions had asked a Paris administrative court on Tuesday to force publication of any ban and suspend it [2]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez asked prefects on Tuesday for "robust" security plans for the "sensitive" day, franceinfo reported, citing an AFP-seen telegram [3]. A CGT map listed 244 protests planned across France for Thursday [3]. Government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon said a repeat of the 17 October unrest was out of the question [1]. A police intelligence note expects 500,000 to 700,000 marchers outside Paris, BFMTV reported, citing RTL [1]. Air traffic controllers, dockers, and rail unions filed strike notices [1]. Magistrates' and lawyers' unions and the Human Rights League accused the state of an "authoritarian shift" in banning marches [1].
Confidence is moderate: the route ban and official statements are reported by two French broadcasters, but the crowd forecast rests on a leaked intelligence note.

items.title: Hungary Opens Communist-Era Secret Police Files to the Public
items.lede: The release fell on the anniversary of the 1956 Soviet invasion, while critics say the files are incomplete and come too late.

sections.text: Hungary opened communist-era secret police files to the public on 4 November, BBC News reported [4][5]. The files identify informants, DW reported [5]. The government says the move will help society heal from 45 years of communist rule [4]. The date marks the day Soviet tanks crushed Hungary's 1956 revolution [4]. Prime Minister Péter Magyar asked people to treat the long-overdue release "with dignity and humanity" [4]. Critics say the files are incomplete and risk sowing division and hurting family members [4].
Confidence is high because BBC News and DW both report the release and the prime minister's remarks.

items.title: EU Report Names Ukraine and Moldova Accession Frontrunners but Splits Their Timelines
items.lede: The European Commission told Ukraine it must speed up rule-of-law reforms to finish talks by 2028, while Moldova aims for early 2028.

sections.text: The European Commission's annual enlargement report on 4 November named Ukraine, Moldova, Montenegro, and Albania the frontrunners among EU candidates, the Kyiv Independent reported [6]. The Commission said it backs Ukraine's goal of closing talks by the end of 2028 but that reforms must accelerate to meet it [6]. It flagged rule-of-law reforms as Ukraine's main hurdle [6]. Moldova told Brussels it could finish talks by early 2028 [7]. Kyiv and Chisinau have so far advanced in tandem, but that is set to end with the expected opening of the final reform clusters in December [7]. Zelensky has opposed separating the two bids [7].
Confidence is high because the Kyiv Independent quotes the Commission's published report and statement.

items.title: Belgium's King Meets Coalition Leaders as a Budget Crisis Shakes the Government
items.lede: Flemish Socialist leader Conner Rousseau told King Philippe his party still wants a budget deal within the current federal coalition.

sections.text: Belgium's King Philippe began receiving leaders of the federal Arizona coalition on Wednesday over a political crisis on the budget, RTBF reported [8]. Conner Rousseau, president of the Flemish Socialists, Vooruit, was the first coalition leader received [8]. Rousseau told the king his party still wants a budget agreement within the current government, RTBF said [8]. He described a "long conversation about the seriousness of the situation" and said it was "now or never" [8].
Confidence is moderate: the meeting and Rousseau's remarks rest on one Belgian public broadcaster's short report.

items.title: Eurozone Inflation Climbs to 4% as Energy Prices Soar
items.lede: Eurostat's flash estimate puts October inflation at its highest since September 2023, driven by energy costs up nearly 21% from a year earlier.

sections.text: Consumer prices in the eurozone rose 4.0% in October from a year earlier, Eurostat said in a flash estimate reported by tagesschau.de [9]. That is the highest rate since September 2023, up from 3.8% in September [9]. Energy prices rose 20.8%, up from 18.9% [9]. Services rose 3.3%, and food, alcohol, and tobacco rose 1.6% [9]. Economists polled by Reuters had expected 4.0% [9]. A KfW economist said rates near 4% could persist while the Iran conflict is unresolved and might ease only in the second quarter of 2027 [9].
Confidence is high because the figures come from Eurostat's official flash estimate.

items.title: Costa Invites EU Leaders to Dublin for a Summit on AI
items.lede: European Council President António Costa has called the bloc's heads of government to Ireland on 13 November to discuss artificial intelligence.

sections.text: European Council President António Costa invited EU leaders to an informal summit in Dublin on 13 November focused on artificial intelligence, the Council said [10]. Leaders will discuss Europe's position in AI with Arthur Mensch, chief executive of Mistral AI, ANSA reported [11]. They will discuss AI's wider impact on society with Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton [11][12]. Lusa reported that Ireland hosts the meeting [12].
Confidence is high because the Council published the invitation and ANSA and Lusa report its contents.

items.title: Greenland's Parliament Ratifies a Security Pact With the US and Denmark
items.lede: The deal opens the way for a larger US military presence on the island and eased pressure from President Trump's annexation threats.

sections.text: Greenland's parliament on Tuesday approved a three-way security and military-access agreement with the United States and Denmark, DW reported [13]. The deal paves the way for an expanded US military presence on the island [13]. Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, and Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed it in September at the UN General Assembly [13]. DW said the deal eased pressure from Trump, who had repeatedly threatened to take control of the self-governing Danish territory [13].
Confidence is high, based on DW reporting of the parliamentary vote.

items.title: France Counts 37 School Staff Hurt in Two Days as Blockades Continue
items.lede: Education Minister Édouard Geffray said his ministry has filed at least 1,000 complaints over violence against school staff since the student movement began.

sections.text: France's Education Ministry said 48 of about 3,700 high schools were blocked at 9:30 a.m. Tuesday [14][15]. The student union USL claimed 500 [15]. Darmanin said more than 1,300 police and gendarmes have been injured in the protests [14]. Paris police had banned a 3 November student march from the Panthéon and offered a Porte de Charenton route [16]. A Paris court rejected a challenge to the ban without a hearing, police said, and several hundred students marched in the Latin Quarter anyway [14]. A national protest day is set for Thursday, 5 November [15]. On Wednesday, the ministry said 19 high schools were blocked at 9:30 a.m. [3]. Geffray told the National Assembly that 37 school staff were injured in the past 48 hours [1]. He said his ministry had filed at least 1,000 complaints over violence against staff since the movement began [1]. The Rhône prefecture said 28 people were arrested there this week for firing fireworks, throwing objects, and setting fires near schools [17]. A school administrator and a police officer were hurt Wednesday, and seven Rhône schools switched to remote classes [17].
Confidence is moderate because the figures come from ministers, prefectures, and live blogs, and the student union disputes the ministry's blockade counts.

items.title: Netherlands Nominates Klaas Knot in the Race to Succeed Lagarde at the ECB
items.lede: The former Dutch central bank chief, a monetary hawk, is seen as a leading candidate ahead of the 6 November nomination deadline.

sections.text: The Netherlands nominated Klaas Knot, the former head of its central bank, to lead the European Central Bank, NOS reported [18]. Finance Minister Eelco Heinen told parliament in The Hague [19]. Knot, 59, ran the Dutch central bank from 2011 to 2025 and favors tight monetary policy, tagesschau.de reported [19]. Christine Lagarde has said she will leave early, in February [19]. The European Union has formally opened the process to replace European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, Euronews reported [20]. Eurogroup President Kyriakos Pierrakakis, Greece's finance minister, asked member states to send nominations by 6 November, a spokesperson said [20]. POLITICO Europe also reported the 6 November deadline [21]. Eurozone finance ministers will review the names at their meeting on 9 November [20]. A candidate needs the backing of at least 16 of the 21 eurozone countries, representing at least 65% of the bloc's population [20]. EU leaders then make the final appointment [20].
Confidence is high because NOS and tagesschau.de report the nomination, and Euronews and POLITICO Europe report the process and deadline.

items.title: Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente Quits Over the Urda Rail Disaster
items.lede: He told Congress no minister could stay after two such crashes in under a year, and he will not run in the early election.

sections.text: Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente resigned on Tuesday, six days after a high-speed train collision near Urda killed at least 69 people, BBC News reported [22]. He announced the decision in Congress after testifying on the 28 October crash and outlining new rail safety measures [22]. Puente cited January's crash on the same line, which killed 46 people [22]. He also withdrew from his party's lists for the early legislative election [22]. The People's Party, Vox, and some government allies had called for him to go [22]. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo will also run the Transport Ministry until the 29 November election [23][24]. Sánchez said Puente's exit helps restore confidence in the railways and in political dignity [23].
Confidence is high, based on BBC reporting of his statement in Congress and POLITICO Europe and El País reporting of Sánchez's announcement.

items.title: Ireland's Prime Minister Plans an Initiative on the Island's Constitutional Future
items.lede: Micheál Martin's move comes as his coalition partner Fine Gael prepares its own blueprint on Irish unity.

sections.text: Ireland's Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, will set up a new initiative on the constitutional future of the island of Ireland, BBC News reported [25]. The move comes as coalition partner Fine Gael prepares to unveil its own blueprint on Irish unity at its party conference in Cork this weekend [25]. Martin outlined the Futures Study Initiative to his Fianna Fáil lawmakers on Tuesday [25][26]. It will examine three scenarios, including a unitary republic and an all-island state with devolved government in Northern Ireland [25][26]. It will invite submissions from every party and produce a report for the government, which will be published [25].
Confidence is high because BBC News and RTÉ both report the plan from Martin's policy paper to his party.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Estonia's Former Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur Quits Politics Before the March Election
items.lede: Pevkur, who left the defense post in September, is one of at least five Reform Party politicians who say they will not run in 2027.

sections.text: Estonia's former Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur said he will not seek reelection in the spring and will leave politics for the private sector, ERR News reported [1]. Pevkur resigned as defense minister in September [1]. He served 25 years in politics and 12 years in government, ERR said [1]. He is one of at least five Reform Party politicians who have said they will not run in the March 2027 national election [1].
Confidence is high because Estonia's public broadcaster reports Pevkur's own statement.

items.title: Lithuania's Prime Minister Orders a Study of a Windfall Tax on Energy Firms
items.lede: Mindaugas Sinkevičius told three ministers to assess fuel, power, and heating profits and propose options urgently.

sections.text: Lithuania's Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius on Wednesday told the energy, finance, and economy ministers to urgently assess energy companies' profits, LRT reported [2]. He asked for proposals on taxing windfall gains [2]. The review covers fuel, electricity, and heating [2]. The ministries will also study what a tax would mean for energy prices and consumers [2]. Sinkevičius said decisions must rest on data given the current geopolitical situation [2].
Confidence is high on the order, which LRT reports from the prime minister's statement.

items.title: Lithuania Expels Three Ukrainians It Says Took Paid Tasks From Hostile Spies
items.lede: The State Security Department said the three got assignments through Telegram and are barred from returning for five years.

sections.text: Lithuania expelled three Ukrainian citizens accused of carrying out paid tasks for "hostile" foreign intelligence services, the State Security Department (VSD) said Wednesday, LRT reported [3]. The three had earlier been declared threats to national security, and their residence permits were revoked [3]. The VSD said they are banned from returning for five years [3]. It said the tasks came through Telegram and other messaging apps [3]. The agency did not name the country behind the tasks in the passages read [3].
Confidence is moderate: the expulsions rest on the security agency's statement relayed by one public broadcaster; the underlying evidence is not public.

items.title: Lithuania's Defense Minister Floats a State Drone Holding Company
items.lede: Robertas Kaunas wants separate Lithuanian makers for attack, interceptor, long-range, and reconnaissance drones under one state-backed group.

sections.text: Lithuania is considering a state-owned drone holding company to speed up military purchases and build its drone industry, Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas told BNS, LRT reported [4]. Kaunas said he wants one Lithuanian maker to build FPV drones, another interceptors, and others long-range and reconnaissance drones [4]. The state would finance the holding, with scientists and universities contributing technology [4].
Confidence is moderate: this is a minister's proposal in one interview, not a government decision.

items.title: Latvia's President Formally Asks Andris Kulbergs to Form a Government
items.lede: President Edgars Rinkēvičs signed the decree after the outgoing cabinet resigned, and both men hope for a new government by the 18 November national holiday.

sections.text: Latvia's President Edgars Rinkēvičs officially nominated Andris Kulbergs, leader of the election-winning United List, for prime minister, LSM reported [5]. Rinkēvičs could sign the decree only after the previous government resigned on 3 November [5]. Kulbergs will continue coalition talks [5]. Both hope to form a government by Latvia's independence day on 18 November [5][6].
Confidence is high because Latvia's public broadcaster reports the signed decree.

items.title: Orlen Weighs Dropping an Upgrade That Could Doom Lithuania's Only Refinery
items.lede: The Polish group's chief said scrapping the Mažeikiai investment would mean accepting a possible shutdown of the Baltic region's only oil refinery.

sections.text: Poland's Orlen is considering abandoning a major upgrade at its Mažeikiai refinery in Lithuania, CEO Ireneusz Fafara told PAP Biznes, LRT reported [7]. The upgrade would extend the plant's life by more than a decade [7]. If it is scrapped, Orlen would have to accept the possibility of closing the Baltic region's only oil refinery [7]. Fafara said the key question is whether Orlen Lietuva can fund the project without help from its Polish parent [7].
Confidence is moderate: the remarks come from one interview relayed by LRT, and no decision has been made.

items.title: Latvian Parliament Refuses to Form Friendship Groups With Russia and Belarus
items.lede: The new Saeima's decision cites Russia's invasion of Ukraine and Belarus letting its territory be used for the attack.

sections.text: Latvia's new parliament, the Saeima, decided not to form parliamentary cooperation groups with Russia and Belarus, LSM reported [8]. The decision says Russia's invasion of Ukraine grossly violates Ukraine's sovereignty and international law [8]. It says Belarus broke its international obligations by letting its territory be used for aggression against Ukraine [8]. The Saeima routinely forms such groups with many countries, and some offer official travel [8].
Confidence is high on the decision, which Latvia's public broadcaster reports from the adopted text.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the Western Balkans

items.title: Bosnian State Police Arrest Four and Seize Forged Europol Badges
items.lede: SIPA's Operation BIG in Sarajevo targeted illicit trade in narcotic drugs, with searches at six locations under a state court order.

sections.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina's State Investigation and Protection Agency (SIPA) arrested four people in the Sarajevo area on Wednesday, the Sarajevo Times reported [1]. The operation, code-named BIG, ran under a Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina order [1]. Suspected offenses include illicit trade and unauthorized production and sale of narcotic drugs [1]. Searches at six locations turned up phones, computers, medicines, and forged official ID cards [1]. Among the forged items was a fake Europol ID card, SIPA said [1].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one outlet's report of the agency's statement.

items.title: EU Tells Serbia's Incoming Government It Has a Chance for a Fresh Start
items.lede: Commissioner Marta Kos said the student movement that beat Vučić can revive Serbia's stalled talks, while Albania trails Montenegro by about a year.

sections.text: Serbia's EU talks could revive if the student movement that beat Vučić's party forms a government that strengthens democracy, the European Commission said, DW reported [2]. "Now Serbia has the chance for a fresh start," Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos told EU lawmakers on Wednesday [2]. The Commission said progress has been slower in North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Serbia [2]. None of the three, nor Kosovo, got an accession roadmap, tagesschau.de reported [3]. The Commission said Albania is about a year behind Montenegro [2]. It said Albania must keep reforming its courts and fighting organized crime and corruption to finish talks by the end of 2027 [2].
Confidence is high because DW and tagesschau.de both report the Commission's published findings and Kos's remarks.

items.title: Kosovo Identifies Three More Victims of Wartime Disappearances
items.lede: Prime Minister Albin Kurti said DNA tests in The Hague matched remains exhumed from sites near Zubin Potok in north Kosovo.

sections.text: Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti confirmed on Tuesday that three more victims of enforced disappearance during the 1998-99 war were identified, Balkan Insight reported [4]. The identifications followed DNA analysis in The Hague [4]. The remains came from Kalluder and Jabuke, villages near Zubin Potok in north Kosovo, where a mass grave was excavated this year [4].
Confidence is moderate: the report rests on the prime minister's statement relayed by one regional outlet.

items.title: Moscow-Bound Air Serbia Flight Carrying Vučić Allies Ordered Back to Belgrade
items.lede: An Air Serbia jet bound for Russia turned around over Lithuania with former intelligence chief Aleksandar Vulin and gas boss Dušan Bajatović aboard.

sections.text: Air Serbia flight JU134 left Belgrade for Moscow at 18:48 CET on 3 November and turned back over southern Lithuania, bne IntelliNews reported, citing N1 [5]. It landed in Belgrade shortly before 22:00 CET [5]. Former intelligence chief Aleksandar Vulin, Srbijagas head Dušan Bajatović, and Serbian People's Party leader Nenad Popović were on board [6][5]. N1 said it was told off the record that Vulin had boarded without security screening [6]. Vulin called the reports lies and a politically motivated campaign against him [6]. Bajatović told N1 he was traveling over gas supplies and payment problems after the Alta Bank case [6][5]. Passengers were screened again and reboarded at about 01:50 CET on 4 November [5]. The airport, police, and prosecutors had made no statement by early 4 November [5].
Confidence is high that the flight turned back with Vulin and Bajatović aboard, which N1 and bne IntelliNews report. The reason rests on unofficial accounts.

items.title: Montenegro Could Finish EU Talks This Year, With Membership Possible in 2028
items.lede: The European Commission said Montenegro could close its remaining chapters by the end of this year and named it the frontrunner among nine candidate countries.

sections.text: Radio Free Europe obtained a draft European Commission plan for Montenegro's EU accession, Albania's CNA reported [7]. Croatia's Jutarnji list said it also obtained the draft, which commissioners are due to adopt Wednesday [8]. Under the plan, Montenegro would close its remaining chapters at conferences in November and December [7][8]. Work on the accession treaty would finish in spring 2027, and the treaty could be signed in June 2027 [7][8]. Montenegro has provisionally closed 21 of 33 chapters [7]. The Commission said the dates are not final and depend on Montenegro meeting the conditions [7]. On Wednesday, the European Commission said Montenegro could close its remaining chapters by the end of this year, subject to member states' agreement [9]. DW and tagesschau.de reported that membership is possible in 2028 [2][3]. Its annual report named Montenegro the frontrunner among nine candidates [2]. Croatia was the last country to join, in 2013 [2].
Confidence is high on the Commission's end-of-year target, which its press release states; the 2028 membership date and June 2027 signing come from media reports and the leaked draft.

items.title: Serbian Prosecutors Detain Alta Bank Owner Over Cash Taken From Its Vault
items.lede: Prosecutors say Davor Macura took about 45 billion dinars from the vault of the bank, whose license Serbia's central bank revoked on Saturday.

sections.text: Serbia's Organized Crime Prosecutor's Office said Monday it had detained Alta Bank's owner and two bank employees, B92 reported [10]. AP named the owner as Davor Macura [11]. Prosecutors said the two employees gave him access to the bank's vault, where he allegedly removed cash [10]. They put the illegal gain at about 45 billion dinars, which AP put at about $428 million [10][11]. The suspects were ordered held for 48 hours [10]. Serbia's central bank revoked Alta Bank's license on Saturday and started bankruptcy proceedings, AP reported [11]. The bank rose under President Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party, which lost the 25 October election, AP said [11]. A Belgrade commercial court opened bankruptcy proceedings against the bank on Tuesday, Balkan Insight reported [12]. Serbia's Deposit Insurance Agency said it will start repaying insured deposits of up to 50,000 euros per depositor within seven working days [12]. Many of the bank's clients are Russians who moved to Serbia, and they have been locked out of their accounts, Balkan Insight said [12].
Confidence is high because the prosecutors' statement and AP both report the detention. The charges are allegations, and Macura has not been charged in court.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the South Caucasus

items.title: Pashinyan Says Armenia Could Formally Apply to Join the EU in 2027 or 2028
items.lede: Armenia's prime minister told Euronews he aims to finish visa liberalization with the EU by 2029 while balancing ties with Russia.

sections.text: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said Armenia could formally apply for EU membership in 2027 or 2028, OC Media reported from his Euronews interview [1]. He said Armenia aims to complete visa liberalization with the EU in 2029 [1]. Moscow and Minsk say EU accession is incompatible with Armenia's membership of the Russia-led Eurasian Economic Union [1]. Pashinyan told Euronews peace with Azerbaijan and the Trump Route corridor give the South Caucasus a "totally new global role" [2].
Confidence is high because Euronews, which conducted the interview, and OC Media report the same remarks.

items.title: EU Report Says Georgia Is a Candidate in Name Only as Backsliding Continues
items.lede: The European Commission warned that Georgia's democratic decline could put its visa-free travel at risk while its accession stays de facto halted.

sections.text: The European Commission said Georgia's accession remains "de facto halted" and noted "continued backsliding" in its 2026 enlargement report on 4 November, Civil Georgia reported [3]. The Commission said Georgia remains "an EU candidate in name only" and continues to forgo the benefits of candidate status [3]. It said the ruling party pursued attacks on democratic principles, the rule of law, and fundamental rights [3]. It said repressive laws have severely curtailed civic space [3]. The report warned that failing to address these concerns puts visa-free travel at risk "more generally" [3]. It said integration could resume if the authorities change course [3]. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Georgia's government is "on a collision course with the European Union" [4]. She said EU foreign ministers will discuss new measures in January and that "everything is on the table" [4]. Asked about sanctions, she said it was too early to tell [4].
Confidence is high because Civil Georgia quotes the Commission's published report.

items.title: Fire Forces Georgia's Opposition-Leaning Formula TV Off the Air
items.lede: Staff trapped by smoke in the Tbilisi business center were led out in small groups, and the channel said the fire is out.

sections.text: A fire at a Tbilisi business center that houses Georgia's opposition-leaning Formula TV forced the channel to suspend broadcasting on Wednesday, Civil Georgia reported [5][6]. Some staff were stuck inside because of heavy smoke [5][6]. Firefighters later led all employees down the stairwell in groups of four, a Formula host told TV Pirveli [5]. Formula TV said the fire had been put out [5]. No cause had been reported by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: two Georgian outlets report the fire, but its cause is unknown.

items.title: Azerbaijan's Draft Budget Trims Special Defense Projects to $2.35 Billion
items.lede: Overall defense and security spending would still rise about 1.2% in 2027, while military housing funds fall 41%.

sections.text: Azerbaijan's draft 2027 budget sets 4 billion manats, about $2.35 billion, for special defense projects, OC Media reported [7]. That is 11.1% less than the 4.5 billion manats set for 2026 [7]. Overall defense and national security spending would rise about 1.2% [7]. Funding for military housing and rent compensation would fall 41.2% [7].
Confidence is moderate: the figures come from the draft budget as reported by one outlet and may change before adoption.

items.title: Armenian Investigators Find No Intent to Kill by an Azerbaijani Soldier Who Crossed In
items.lede: The soldier, detained in October after shooting and wounding a woman in her Syunik home, still faces charges including grievous bodily harm.

sections.text: Armenia's Investigative Committee chief, Artur Poghosyan, said the Azerbaijani soldier who crossed into Armenia in October had no intention of killing anyone, OC Media reported [8]. The committee detained soldier Nasimi Musayev on 1 October [8]. He is accused of shooting and wounding Ani Avetisyan in her home in Shaki village, Syunik province [8]. Charges include grievous bodily harm with a weapon, illegal border crossing, and weapons smuggling [8].
Confidence is moderate: the finding is the investigator's statement relayed by one outlet.

items.title: Georgian Premier Kobakhidze Rejects EU Criticism at a Brussels Summit
items.lede: He defended the ruling party's bid to ban five opposition parties and challenged the European Commission to a debate a day before its enlargement reports.

sections.text: Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze dismissed European criticism of Georgia's democratic record in an interview at Euronews' EU Enlargement Summit in Brussels on 3 November, Civil Georgia reported [9]. He invited European Commission officials to a "debate" and said Georgia still wants to join the EU "with dignity" [9]. He defended Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban five opposition parties [9]. The summit came a day before the Commission published its annual enlargement reports, including one on Georgia [9]. Euronews, which conducted the interview, also reported his remarks [10].
Confidence is high because Civil Georgia and Euronews, which conducted the interview, report the remarks.

items.title: Merz Will Skip the World Leaders' Session at the UN Climate Summit in Turkey
items.lede: A German government spokesman cited other commitments, and climate groups called the decision a taboo break and an embarrassment.

sections.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz will not attend the leaders' meeting at the UN climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, next week, the Stuttgarter Zeitung reported [1]. A government spokesman in Berlin cited "other commitments" and gave no details [1]. Luisa Neubauer of Fridays for Future called it an "absolute taboo-breaking" move [1]. Greenpeace called it an embarrassment [1]. Nearly 200 countries meet in Antalya for two weeks from Monday [1].
Confidence is high on the decision, which the paper reports from the government spokesman.

items.title: BMW's Profit Falls Nearly 15% as China Sales Slump
items.lede: Germany's BMW issued a profit warning for the fourth quarter, citing weak China sales, severance costs, and the early end of older models.

sections.text: Germany's BMW earned 1.45 billion euros after tax in the third quarter, almost 15% less than a year earlier, tagesschau.de reported [2]. The Munich carmaker issued a profit warning on Tuesday evening for the fourth quarter [2]. The main driver is its shrinking China business [2]. Costly severance payments and the early end of older models also hurt results [2]. The Guardian linked the warning to the cost of a plan for 8,000 job cuts [3].
Confidence is high because the figures come from BMW's own results, reported by tagesschau.de and the Guardian.

items.title: Pistorius Says Every Country Favors Its Own Arms Makers, Not Just Germany
items.lede: Germany's defense minister answered the European Parliament's defense chair, Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann, at the Berlin Security Conference.

sections.text: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius pushed back on Wednesday against criticism that Germany puts its own arms industry ahead of European cooperation, POLITICO Europe reported [4]. He spoke at the Berlin Security Conference [4]. He was answering Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann, chair of the European Parliament's defense committee [4]. She had accused Germany of buying too much from its own manufacturers [4]. Pistorius said every country backs joint projects in public but favors its own industry "when push comes to shove" [4].
Confidence is high on the exchange, which POLITICO Europe reports from the conference; it is one outlet's account.

items.title: Baden-Württemberg Coalition Sets Aside 1 Billion Euros for Local Climate Projects
items.lede: The Green-CDU state government will give municipalities 200 million euros a year through 2031 for school renovations, heat protection, and flood defenses.

sections.text: Baden-Württemberg's Green-CDU coalition will give municipalities 200 million euros a year through 2031 for climate protection, the Stuttgarter Zeitung reported [5]. The total of 1 billion euros is called the "climate billion" [5]. The budget commission put 200 million euros into the 2027 budget and secured the rest in financial planning, the Greens in the state parliament said [5]. The money covers energy renovation of daycare centers and schools, green spaces, heat protection, and protection against heavy rain [5].
Confidence is high because the paper reports the coalition's own announcement.

items.title: Germany's Top Court Hears an Expelled AfD Lawmaker's Challenge
items.lede: Jan Wenzel Schmidt was thrown out of the AfD's Bundestag group after he raised nepotism claims against fellow lawmakers.

sections.text: Germany's Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe is hearing a challenge by AfD lawmaker Jan Wenzel Schmidt to his expulsion from the party's parliamentary group, tagesschau.de reported [6]. Schmidt was expelled after he started a debate about nepotism in the AfD earlier this year [6]. Several AfD lawmakers were reported to have hired relatives of other AfD lawmakers in their offices [6]. Many cases came from the Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt branches [6].
Confidence is moderate: the hearing is reported by one public broadcaster, and no ruling had been reported by the cutoff.

items.title: Hackers Heat a Bavarian Butcher's Cold Stores to 150 C as German Cases Grow
items.lede: Police in Regensburg said the attack on a butcher in the Neustadt an der Waldnaab district caused damage in the tens of thousands of euros.

sections.text: Hackers switched refrigeration systems from cooling to heating overnight at several supermarkets in Germany, tagesschau.de reported [7]. Affected stores included two CAP markets in Wuppertal and Wetter, a Rewe in Raesfeld, and Edeka stores in Lilienthal and Reisbach [7]. The CAP operator told the dpa news agency that the attack targeted the company that remotely maintains the systems [7]. Large amounts of food had to be thrown out [7]. Similar attacks hit supermarkets in other European countries [7]. On Wednesday, police in Regensburg said hackers also hit several cold stores of a butcher in Bavaria's Neustadt an der Waldnaab district [8]. The attackers changed settings overnight into Monday so the rooms heated up to 150 C [8]. Police put the damage in the tens of thousands of euros and said early detection prevented worse losses [8].
Confidence is high, based on public-broadcaster reporting with named stores, an operator's confirmation to dpa, and a police statement.

items.title: Draft Report Projects a 4.1% Rise in German Pensions in 2027
items.lede: A pension of 1,000 euros would rise by 41 euros a month, though final figures are not due until March.

sections.text: Germany's government expects statutory pensions to rise 4.1% in 2027, according to a draft pension insurance report seen by ARD, tagesschau.de reported [9]. A pension of 1,000 euros would rise by 41 euros a month [9]. Pensions rose 4.2% this year [9]. The estimate is preliminary, and exact figures are due in March [9]. The contribution rate is set to stay at 18.6% next year and reach 20% in 2030 [9].
Confidence is high on the draft's figures as reported by the public broadcaster; the estimate itself is preliminary.
